simple.meaning: עִיט (ʻîyṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to swoop down upon (literally or figuratively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 14:32. Its contexts include blood, death, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִיט (H5860).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עִיט (ʻîyṭ) / H5860 is traced through 1 Samuel 14:32, 1 Samuel 15:19, 1 Samuel 25:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5860. iyt [ עִיט ] verb scream, shriek (Arabic , II. scream, scold , screaming, scolding , Frey Dozy ii. 195 ; Syriac anger, reviling ); — only Qal Imperfect 3masculine singular בָּהֶם וַיָּ֫עַט 1Sam 25:14 and he screamed at them (of Nabal). [ עִיט ] verb denominative dart greedily (like a bird of prey); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיַּ֫עַט Qr (Kt:erroneous ויעשׂ ) 1Sam 14:32 and the people darted greedily upon the spoil ( אֶלהַֿשָּׁלָל , so 2 masculine singular וַתַּ֫עַט 15:19 (on forms see Ges § 72 f f.).
